atoms.text: This guide configures ThumbForge, an image resizing service, to read source photographs from the bucket catalog-media and write resized renditions back to the same bucket. ThumbForge reads objects under the prefix originals/ and writes JPEG renditions at 128, 512, and 1024 pixels wide under the prefix thumbnails/. Access is granted only through an IAM role that ThumbForge assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named thumbforge-processing-role with a trust policy that allows the ThumbForge service principal, thumbforge.svc.example, to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:GetObject on catalog-media/originals/*, storage:PutObject on catalog-media/thumbnails/*, and storage:ListBucket on catalog-media with a prefix condition of originals/. In the ThumbForge job configuration, set the execution role to the role's resource name so the service obtains temporary credentials for each resize job. Leave the existing bucket policy as it is; it continues to govern all other principals. To verify, upload one test image to originals/ and confirm that three objects appear under thumbnails/. The access log entries for those writes should show the assumed-role session as the requester.

This guide configures ThumbForge, an image resizing service, to read source photographs from the bucket catalog-media and write resized renditions back to the same bucket. ThumbForge reads objects under the prefix originals/ and writes JPEG renditions at 128, 512, and 1024 pixels wide under the prefix thumbnails/. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the ThumbForge service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the policy of catalog-media with the principal thumbforge.svc.example and an Allow effect. In that statement, allow storage:GetObject on catalog-media/originals/*, storage:PutObject on catalog-media/thumbnails/*, and storage:ListBucket on catalog-media with a prefix condition of originals/. In the ThumbForge job configuration, leave the execution role field empty so the service sends requests to the bucket as its own service principal. Do not attach any identity-based policy; the bucket policy is the only place these permissions are defined. To verify, upload one test image to originals/ and confirm that three objects appear under thumbnails/. The access log entries for those writes should show the ThumbForge service principal as the requester.

This guide gives ReelPack, a video transcoding service, access to the bucket studio-masters so it can read mezzanine files and write streaming outputs. ReelPack reads .mov files under the prefix mezzanine/ and writes HLS playlists (.m3u8) and media segments (.ts) for three bitrate renditions under the prefix hls/. Access is granted only through an IAM role that ReelPack assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named reelpack-transcode-role whose trust policy lets the service principal reelpack.svc.example assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:GetObject on studio-masters/mezzanine/*, and storage:PutObject and storage:AbortMultipartUpload on studio-masters/hls/*. Add storage:ListBucket on studio-masters, restricted to the prefix mezzanine/, so ReelPack can enumerate pending inputs. Register the role's resource name in the ReelPack pipeline settings, and the service will request temporary credentials at the start of every transcoding job. Because the bucket policy is untouched, no existing bucket-level rule needs to be reviewed. Confirm the setup by transcoding a 30-second test clip and checking that a master playlist and its segments appear under hls/.

ReelPack reads .mov files under the prefix mezzanine/ and writes HLS playlists (.m3u8) and media segments (.ts) for three bitrate renditions under the prefix hls/. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the ReelPack service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the policy of studio-masters that names the principal reelpack.svc.example. The statement allows storage:GetObject on studio-masters/mezzanine/*, and storage:PutObject and storage:AbortMultipartUpload on studio-masters/hls/*. Add storage:ListBucket on studio-masters, restricted to the prefix mezzanine/, so ReelPack can enumerate pending inputs. In the ReelPack pipeline settings, leave the role field blank, and the service will send each request as its own principal during every transcoding job. Because the permissions live in the bucket policy, review that policy for conflicting Deny statements. Confirm the setup by transcoding a 30-second test clip and checking that a master playlist and its segments appear under hls/.

This guide enables ScanLeaf, an optical character recognition service, to process scanned records stored in the bucket records-intake. ScanLeaf reads PDF files under the prefix scans/ and writes one JSON file per document, containing page-level text and confidence scores, under the prefix text/. Access is granted only through an IAM role that ScanLeaf assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named scanleaf-ocr-role with a trust policy that names the service principal scanleaf.svc.example as the entity allowed to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:GetObject on records-intake/scans/* and storage:PutObject on records-intake/text/*. Include storage:ListBucket on records-intake with a prefix condition of scans/ so the service can discover new files. Set the role's maximum session duration to one hour, which covers the longest expected batch of about 20 concurrent workers. Enter the role's resource name in the ScanLeaf batch configuration. Verify by submitting one three-page scan and confirming that a single JSON file with three page entries is written to text/.

This guide enables ScanLeaf, an optical character recognition service, to process scanned records stored in the bucket records-intake. ScanLeaf reads PDF files under the prefix scans/ and writes one JSON file per document, containing page-level text and confidence scores, under the prefix text/. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the ScanLeaf service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the policy of records-intake that names scanleaf.svc.example as the principal. The statement allows storage:GetObject on records-intake/scans/* and storage:PutObject on records-intake/text/*. Include storage:ListBucket on records-intake with a prefix condition of scans/ so the service can discover new files. Because no role is involved, there is no session duration to configure, and the roughly 20 concurrent workers send requests as the service principal. Leave the role field in the ScanLeaf batch configuration empty. Verify by submitting one three-page scan and confirming that a single JSON file with three page entries is written to text/.

This guide allows VoxLine, a speech transcription service, to read call recordings from the bucket call-recordings and write transcripts back to it. VoxLine reads .wav files under the prefix audio/ and writes a WebVTT caption file and a JSON transcript with word timestamps for each recording under the prefix transcripts/. Access is granted only through an IAM role that VoxLine assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named voxline-transcribe-role and set its trust policy to allow the service principal voxline.svc.example to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:GetObject on call-recordings/audio/* and storage:PutObject on call-recordings/transcripts/*. The same policy should allow storage:ListBucket on call-recordings with a prefix condition of audio/. In the VoxLine project settings, specify the role's resource name as the service role. VoxLine then requests short-lived credentials whenever a transcription task starts. Test the setup by placing a 60-second recording in audio/ and confirming that both a .vtt file and a .json file appear under transcripts/.

This guide allows VoxLine, a speech transcription service, to read call recordings from the bucket call-recordings and write transcripts back to it. VoxLine reads .wav files under the prefix audio/ and writes a WebVTT caption file and a JSON transcript with word timestamps for each recording under the prefix transcripts/. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the VoxLine service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the policy of call-recordings whose principal is voxline.svc.example. The statement allows storage:GetObject on call-recordings/audio/* and storage:PutObject on call-recordings/transcripts/*. The same statement should allow storage:ListBucket on call-recordings with a prefix condition of audio/. In the VoxLine project settings, leave the service role unset so that the service calls the storage service directly as its own principal. No credentials are issued through role assumption, and the bucket policy is the single source of these permissions. Test the setup by placing a 60-second recording in audio/ and confirming that both a .vtt file and a .json file appear under transcripts/.

This guide connects PageShift, a document conversion service, to the bucket contracts-drafts so it can turn word-processor files into PDFs. PageShift reads .docx files under the prefix drafts/ and writes PDF/A-2b files with embedded fonts under the prefix pdf/, using the same base file name. Access is granted only through an IAM role that PageShift assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named pageshift-convert-role with a trust policy that permits the service principal pageshift.svc.example to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:GetObject on contracts-drafts/drafts/* and storage:PutObject on contracts-drafts/pdf/*. Add storage:ListBucket on contracts-drafts with a prefix condition of drafts/ so that queued conversions can be listed. Provide the role's resource name in the PageShift workspace settings under the execution identity field. Any conversion request that targets another prefix will fail, because the role's policy does not list it. To verify, upload a sample .docx file to drafts/ and confirm that a PDF with the same base name appears in pdf/ within a minute.

This guide lets MarkPress, a watermarking service, read unmarked press photos from the bucket press-photos and write watermarked copies to the same bucket. MarkPress reads JPEG files under the prefix raw/, reads a single overlay image at config/watermark.png, and writes the composited JPEGs under the prefix marked/. Access is granted only through an IAM role that MarkPress assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named markpress-stamp-role and add a trust policy that allows the service principal markpress.svc.example to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:GetObject on press-photos/raw/* and press-photos/config/watermark.png, and storage:PutObject on press-photos/marked/*. Do not grant write access to raw/ or config/, so the source files and the overlay cannot be modified by the service. Enter the role's resource name in the MarkPress stamping profile. The service assumes the role at the start of each batch and releases the credentials when the batch finishes. Verify by running a batch on one photo and checking that marked/ contains a JPEG with the overlay in the lower-right corner.

This guide lets MarkPress, a watermarking service, read unmarked press photos from the bucket press-photos and write watermarked copies to the same bucket. MarkPress reads JPEG files under the prefix raw/, reads a single overlay image at config/watermark.png, and writes the composited JPEGs under the prefix marked/. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the MarkPress service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the policy of press-photos that names the principal markpress.svc.example. The statement allows storage:GetObject on press-photos/raw/* and press-photos/config/watermark.png, and storage:PutObject on press-photos/marked/*. Do not grant write access to raw/ or config/, so the source files and the overlay cannot be modified by the service. Leave the role field in the MarkPress stamping profile blank. The service sends each request directly as its principal, and no credentials are issued per batch. Verify by running a batch on one photo and checking that marked/ contains a JPEG with the overlay in the lower-right corner.

This guide gives UnpackBay, an archive extraction service, access to the bucket partner-drops, where partners deliver zipped asset bundles. UnpackBay reads .zip files of up to 5 GB under the prefix inbound/ and writes each contained file under extracted/<archive-name>/, preserving the internal directory layout. Access is granted only through an IAM role that UnpackBay assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named unpackbay-extract-role with a trust policy that allows the service principal unpackbay.svc.example to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:GetObject on partner-drops/inbound/*, and storage:PutObject and storage:AbortMultipartUpload on partner-drops/extracted/*. Add storage:ListBucket on partner-drops with a prefix condition of inbound/ so the service can detect new archives. Set the role in the UnpackBay intake rule by entering its resource name. Because large entries are written with multipart uploads, the abort permission lets the service clean up failed extractions. Test with a small archive containing two nested folders and confirm that the same folder structure appears under extracted/.

This guide authorizes RedactLine, a document redaction service, to work with case files in the bucket legal-review. RedactLine reads PDF files under the prefix incoming/, writes redacted PDFs under the prefix redacted/, and writes a CSV report of redaction counts per page under the prefix reports/. Access is granted only through an IAM role that RedactLine assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named redactline-process-role with a trust policy that names the service principal redactline.svc.example as allowed to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:GetObject on legal-review/incoming/*, and storage:PutObject on legal-review/redacted/* and legal-review/reports/*. Add storage:ListBucket on legal-review with a prefix condition of incoming/. In the RedactLine rule set, enter the role's resource name as the processing role, and each redaction job will use temporary credentials from that role. The role has no permission to delete objects, so originals in incoming/ remain in place after processing. Confirm the setup by submitting one test PDF and checking that a redacted PDF and a CSV report appear under their respective prefixes.
